newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. official attacks Cuba on press freedom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official attacks Cuba on press freedom.

text.p: A senior U.S. official attacked Cuba for restricting press freedom on Monday, shortly after CNN became the first U.S. media to broadcast from a permanent bureau on the island in 28 years.
"There is no press freedom at all," Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs Jeffrey Davidow said at an international press freedom conference in Panama City.
"The United States' commitment to a peaceful transition to democracy in Cuba includes support for the open flow of information," he said.

Cuba gave Cable News Network (CNN), an Atlanta-based division of Time Warner Inc., permission to open a bureau in November. CNN is the first U.S. news organisation with a permanent bureau on the Communist-ruled island since 1969.
The cable network began broadcasts from its new bureau in Havana on Monday.
But the U.S. government believes Cuba's President Fidel Castro is still too tough on the press.

"The fact that Castro still intends to limit the number of foreign media and prevent international media from distributing information within Cuba itself is a testament to the Cuban government's fear of a free press," he said.
The Clinton Administration has granted permission to nine other U.S. news organisations to apply to operate in Cuba, but only CNN has been authorised by the Cuban government.
The other media are ABC, CBS, Univision, the Miami Herald, Dow Jones News Services, Cuba Info, the Chicago Tribune and the Sun-Sentinel of Fort Laudrdale, Florida.
